title: Remembrance — killed for faith / race / ethnicity, a sourced memorial record
summary: A continuously-updatable memorial dashboard of people killed for their faith, race or ethnicity — 3-lens toggle, grouped bars, charts (donut + per-group bars + by-year + era), a dated timeline with NAMED PERPETRATORS, by-country deaths + persecution-severity, and a methodology section that presents the counter-evidence. Timetable theme + rainbow bar. Deployed on Cloudflare + git (github.com/Hallalu/remembrance).

tasks.desc: ~24 sourced searches: Open Doors, Pew, USCIRF, UN, MSF, PLOS, ICTY, HRW, ACLED, EJI, Yad Vashem — ranges + caveats
Timetable-theme dashboard; 3 lenses; charts; timeline w/ perpetrators; by-country deaths+severity; Before-1900→2026 era; per-day; print/PDF
Feature-by-feature browser verification (all 3 lenses, charts, filters, timeline, print); deployed Cloudflare + pushed to git

features: Charts: donut share + per-group bars + Open-Doors by-year + deaths-by-era
Timeline with named perpetrators + interfaith/sectarian/ideological tags
findings: The 'killed for their religion' framing is genuinely contested — esp. Nigeria: ACLED/HRW find farmer-herder conflict & banditry kill all faiths, not purely religious persecution. Flagged per-entry.
Open Doors' method is externally audited but criticised as 'home-made' with hard attribution + an auditor tied to its research arm; presented as advocacy-linked estimate, not a census.
'White genocide' is a debunked white-nationalist conspiracy theory (SPLC) — included only documented events (Boer camps, Haiti 1804) and stated the myth plainly.
No faith or ethnicity is only victim or only perpetrator — Orthodox Christian forces (Srebrenica), Hindu mobs (1984), Buddhist-majority military (Rohingya), Hutu/Tutsi both directions.
insights: A critique is a claim too: verified the critic, not just the source; kept wide ranges; excluded the most contested from totals; never invented a restriction.
Reusable pattern: one render layer + datasets keyed identically = an N-lens toggle with zero per-lens rendering code.
